notes: Closed named OSM raceway retained as a course candidate. Named-layout association requires review.
Source way order and shared node IDs are retained. No nearby endpoints are joined and no reference boundaries are read.
Some source ways lack one-way direction tags. Travel direction is provisional.

source.name: Mapzen Terrain Tiles
attribution: Global elevation data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey and NOAA.

sources.notes: Road height is sampled from the existing approximately 22 m terrain raster and compressed to a 0.5 m interpolation tolerance relative to those samples; this is not road-surface survey accuracy. Station distances use the mapped trace, not an official length measurement. The saved start gate sets the simulation origin. Curbs and bend labels are geometry-based illustrations, not extracted from imagery or verified real curb locations; widths, heights and colours are assumed. Banking is unknown and assumed zero. Source border coordinates retain their separate feature-level licence; invalid cross-sections are interpolated. Imagery is an external display resource subject to provider terms; no image bytes are included.

supersedes.reason: Two disjoint original-source artifacts are removed: six vertices in a numerical self-crossing loop, with maximum chord deviation about 0.033 m, and 41 vertices following transverse paint across the straight. The raw review image and local overlays were viewed. The image cannot resolve the numerical loop; its correction is independently bounded geometrically by a two-metre chord and ten-centimetre maximum deviation. Every retained coordinate, original border property, trace, timing and terrain is preserved. Imagery supports only local pavement interpretation and retains separate review rights; remaining source geometry is unverified.

borderInference.note: Reviewed deletion of the pinned source vertices only. Every retained coordinate and original border property is unchanged. Each paint-line group has a near return and bounded local excursion. Any numerical-loop group replaces an actual self-crossing with a chord at most two metres long and at most ten centimetres from every deleted point. The image supports local pavement interpretation but cannot resolve subpixel loops; this is not a new edge extraction or validation of the remaining source geometry.
